newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE flax ends limit up on tight stocks, StatsCan.
newsitem.headline: WCE flax ends limit up on tight stocks, StatsCan.

text.p: WCE flaxseed futures ended up the C$10 a tonne limit in old crop on tight stocks while new crop rose on a reduction in seeding intentions, traders said.

"Commercials were covering shorts on tight stocks, there's nothing out there, and new crop's up on StatsCan," a trader said. Statistics Canada Friday forecast flax area at 2.07 million acres, down from April's estimate of 2.28 million.
July and September rose C$10 to $337.90 and $311.50 each while November was up $4 at $304.90. July-Nov $28. Daily trading limits were expanded to C$15 a tonne for three days.
"Crushers bought the back of canola late, locals covered July and November shorts ahead of the weekend and on StatsCan and funds bought July-Nov and July-Aug," a trader said.

July ended up $2.20 to $383 as UGG bought, all other months were down $0.50 to $2.10 with November down $1.30 to $356.30. July WCE futures crush margin fell to -3.14 Friday from +1.67 Thursday. About 800 July-Nov spread at $26.50, 200 Nov-Mar $5.50, 400 Sep-Nov $0.50, 300 July-Aug $6, Nov-Jan $4. Volume was 5,610 lots, or 112,200 tonnes, with 425 hedge lots.
July feed wheat lost $0.40 to $149.20 on commercial liquidation, December rose $0.10 to $153.70. About 50 July-Oct spread at $3.50. Volume was 650 lots.
July western barley lost $1.20 to $123 after setting a new low at 122.60 on long liquidation, October fell $0.30 to $127.30. About 1,000 July-Oct spread from $3.50 to $4.50.
Commercials bought 25 December oats up US$1 to US$109.
RBC-DS and UGG bought 90 December feed pea contracts down US$3.70 to US$174.30, a trader said.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, peas.)
